text: Discuss articles: Every article card now has a comments section. Share a take, a critique, or how a study changes your practice, and see what colleagues think.

Weekly email: That's this email! Every Saturday you'll get 3 suggested articles to read. You can turn it off anytime with the link at the bottom, or under "Email notification settings" at the top of the site.
All Studies is complete: It now lists every article that scored above 3, in every specialty, instead of only the top 100. Tap "Show more" at the bottom to keep going.
Login fix: Fixed a problem where, after an app update, you could find yourself signed in to a colleague's account. You may be asked to sign in again once.
Tidier specialty filter: On All Studies, the specialty list now only shows specialties that actually have articles, so you won't land on an empty page.

Steadier scores: Points for study size (500+ participants) and for top journals (NEJM, Lancet, JAMA and others with an impact factor of 25 or more) are now given by fixed rules, so the same kind of article always gets the same points. Fewer relevant articles are wrongly left out because of a word in their title.

Newest first in My Library: Your Want to Read and Read lists now show the most recently published articles at the top, and a new "Published" filter lets you narrow them to the past week, month, 3 months or year. Every article you've saved now shows up, including older ones that were sometimes missing.

"Why it matters" on article cards: New studies now get a short big-picture line instead of the Clinical Bottom Line: what earlier studies on the same question mostly showed, and what this study adds. It's written from the abstracts of earlier studies, mostly from the article's own reference list, and you can open "Based on…" to see them. Articles where it can't be written keep their Clinical Bottom Line.

Open-label extensions scored fairly: Long-term open-label extensions of randomized trials (like the HELIOS-B extension) now get 1 point for study type instead of 0, and aren't also marked down as a sub-analysis. This applies to newly scored articles.

Your library stays put: Saved articles, key-study marks and article discussions no longer disappear when the app is updated. Trending now counts only articles colleagues actually saved in the last two weeks.
Forgot your password?: The sign-in page now has a "Forgot password?" link. It emails you a link to choose a new password, so nobody gets locked out.
Suggestion Box: Have an idea for the app, or something that bugs you? The new Suggestion Box in the side menu sends it straight to Gil. You can send it anonymously.
